newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - BTPs vulnerable while stuck under 126.25.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - BTPs vulnerable while stuck under 126.25.

text.p: BTPs are stuck in a corrective phase and while they are trapped under 126.25 they remain vulnerable to the downside, technical analysts said on Friday.
"We have to watch the 126.25 level which seems to be a very, very important Elliot resistance," said Chase technical analyst Guenter Redeker.
"If the market remains below that, it's still vulnerable to the downside so we have to regard current price activity as corrective."
By 0854 GMT, the June BTP was up 46 basis points at 125.57, after approaching the key psychological level of 126.00 earlier.
One analyst at an Italian bank said this 126.00 level would be hard to crack on Friday.

"I think we will have a positive day today, but the 126.00 barrier will not be easy to break in the very near term, as it is a retracement of the main trend since July last year and also a key psychological level," he said. He said above that, 126.20 to 126.40 was a strong barrier, followed by a further cap at 127.20 to 127.40.
The analyst put solid support around 125.20. "I wouldn't expect that support to break, but if it does, 125.00 would be a buying opportunity," he said.
Redeker put minor support at 125.60, then 125.25, followed by 124.40.

He said the June BTP contract had built a third Elliot wave top at 131.80 and was currently in a fourth wave correction. Elliot wave theory holds that the market moves in repetitive patterns, moving in five waves one way followed by a three wave correction.

"The move from 130.80 to 123.60 has been seen as this week's cycle low as part of a c-wave," said Redeker. "So there's some evidence that current price action above 123.60 is just a minor fourth wave correction within a c-wave down."
Redeker said this implied limited upside potential to a maximum of 126.25.
"If we see a rally above 126.25 today there would be some evidence that the c-wave is complete...and the market would be ready for significant upside potential," Redeker added.
